explanation:
## What a US tourist visa (B1/B2) really costs

Applying for a US tourist visa involves more than a single payment. This calculator breaks down every cost involved — from the official fee to local out-of-pocket expenses — so you can budget accurately before starting the process.

---

### The MRV fee: the only fixed, universal cost

The **MRV Fee (Machine Readable Visa Fee)** is **USD 185 per person**, regardless of your country of origin, age, or nonimmigrant visa type. Every applicant pays it before the consular interview, through the payment system enabled by the US embassy in each country.

**Critical points about this fee:**
- It is **non-refundable**, even if your visa is denied, you cancel the appointment, or you don't show up.
- The validity of the MRV payment varies: in some countries the receipt expires after one year if no interview is scheduled; check the specific conditions at your consulate.
- It is paid in local currency or by bank transfer depending on the enabled system (in Argentina, for example, it's paid in pesos at the exchange rate set by the authorized bank at the time of payment, not at the general official rate).

---

### How the estimated total is calculated

The calculator takes the **MRV Fee in USD** as its base and converts it to local currency using the exchange rate you enter. It then adds an estimate of the typical **local out-of-pocket expenses**:

| Item | Estimated range |
|---|---|
| Passport photos (5x5 cm / 2x2 inch format) | Low |
| Photocopies and document certifications | Low-medium |
| Certified translations (if applicable) | Medium-high |
| Travel to the embassy/consulate | Variable |
| Visa agents or processing agencies (optional) | High |

The result is an **indicative total cost**. The only exact, universal figure is the MRV Fee; the rest depends on your city, your particular documentation, and whether you handle the process yourself or hire professional help.

---

### What this calculator does NOT include

These costs are real, but they're not part of the visa process itself:

- **Travel insurance**: Not required for the B1/B2 visa, but recommended and sometimes required by airlines or accommodations. Costs vary.
- **A valid passport**: If you need to renew it before applying for the visa, budget for that separately.
- **ESTA (Electronic System for Travel Authorization)**: Applies only to citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries, not to those applying for a B1/B2. They are separate systems and don't overlap.
- **Flights and accommodation in the US**: Unrelated to the consular process.
- **Third-party expedited visa services**: Private companies offer help preparing the application (DS-160, etc.), but they have no special access to the consular system and cannot guarantee approval.

---

### Common budgeting mistakes

**1. Assuming a denial costs nothing.** The MRV Fee is lost if the visa is denied. For a second application, you must pay it again.

**2. Not accounting for the exchange rate at the time of payment.** If your country's system processes the MRV in local currency, the amount in pesos (or soles, or bolívars) may differ from your calculation if there's a currency gap or the authorized bank applies a specific rate.

**3. Confusing "valid for 10 years" with "10-year stays."** The B1/B2 visa is usually issued with 10-year validity and multiple entries, but **the length of each stay is determined by the immigration officer at the port of entry**, generally up to 6 months per visit. They are two different things.

**4. Not updating the DS-160 if your circumstances change.** The DS-160 form (the online application) is part of the process and must reflect your actual situation at the time of the interview. Errors or omissions can lead to delays or denials.

---

### Context on the B1/B2 visa

The B1/B2 visa covers **temporary visits** for tourism, family visits, medical treatment, business meetings, or conferences. It does not authorize you to work or study in the US (that's what the F-1, H-1B, and other visas are for).

Approval rates vary significantly by the applicant's country of origin. The consular officer mainly assesses whether the applicant has **sufficient ties to their country of residence** (job, family, property) to guarantee their return. There is no automatic approval formula: two similar profiles can get different outcomes.

---

### Practical tip

Before paying the MRV Fee, check **appointment availability at your consulate**. In some countries wait times exceed 6 to 18 months. The payment does not reserve a slot; the appointment is scheduled separately in the local embassy's system.

Official reference source: [travel.state.gov](https://travel.state.gov) — United States Department of State.

faq.q: How much does a US B1/B2 tourist visa cost?
faq.a: The MRV (visa application fee) is $185 USD per person. Total cost also includes processing fees, passport photos, document translations, and any additional services.
The Machine Readable Visa (MRV) fee is the official visa application fee set by the US Department of State. It costs $185 USD per applicant and is non-refundable.

faq.q: How long is a B1/B2 visa valid?
faq.a: If approved, a B1/B2 visa is typically valid for 10 years with unlimited entries. Your actual stay in the US per visit is determined by the immigration officer (usually up to 6 months).
Yes, an in-person interview at the US embassy or consulate is mandatory for most B1/B2 applicants. You'll schedule it online through the official visa appointment system.

faq.q: What documents do I need for a US tourist visa?
faq.a: Required documents typically include: valid passport, completed DS-160 form, visa fee receipt, appointment confirmation, passport-style photo, proof of financial support, and evidence of ties to your home country (employment, property, family).

faq.q: How long does the B1/B2 visa application take?
faq.a: Processing time varies by consulate. You may receive a decision same-day or wait several days to weeks. Standard processing typically takes 3-5 business days after your interview.
The DS-160 is the Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application required for all B1/B2 applicants. It's completed and submitted online through the State Department website and takes 20-30 minutes to fill out.

faq.q: Do I need a US visa to visit the United States?
faq.a: It depends on your citizenship. Citizens of 40 visa-waiver countries can enter the US without a visa for up to 90 days. Citizens of all other countries must apply for a B1/B2 tourist visa.

faq.q: Can I extend my B1/B2 visa stay in the United States?
faq.a: You can request an extension by filing Form I-539 with USCIS before your authorized stay expires. Extensions are granted on a case-by-case basis and require valid reasons.
